# META-INSIGHTS — about the optimization PROCESS itself (this run)

Not about the capability — about HOW this run is searching for it: which strategies/edit classes/algorithms are helping vs stalling, and what to try next iteration. Update at the end of the run at minimum; sooner if a plateau or a clear strategy shift is worth recording now. Structure each addition as:

    ## Iteration <id> (or 'run so far')
    - Strategy tried, and whether it moved val (cite LEDGER rows):
    - Plateau/stall signal, if any, and the lever switched to:
    - What to try next iteration:

## Iteration cand_0001 (seed → first candidate)
- Strategy tried: fan out parallel read-only subagents (one per failure cluster + one that
  read the actual scorer source), then merge many small, scoped, additive prose edits into one
  candidate. Covered all 6 failing + 2 flaky tasks with 6 distinct lever types (ordered
  checklist, worked example, method/procedure, 3 knowledge rules). Not yet scored.
- Highest-value move: READING THE SCORER before writing the output-contract edits. It flipped
  two intuitions — number-as-text is NOT a failure (coerced to float), and a real time is graded
  trimmed to HH:MM — so I scoped the typed-value rule to dates/times only and avoided a wasted
  "numbers must be numeric" edit. Grounding contract edits in the grader, not the old prompt, is
  the lever to keep using.
- Biggest latent risk to watch: a global "use openpyxl in place" steer can perturb a passing
  task that legitimately uses pandas (48745). Mitigated by naming its exact header=None path in
  the rule; if the candidate is rejected net-zero, that steer is the first suspect to rescope.
- What to try next iteration: read the RESULT stamp to attribute Δ per task; if a flaky task
  (250-20/262-17) persists, switch from a knowledge rule to a worked copyable code example for
  that specific operation (stable-sort / dedup-and-shift), since the reader is mid-strong and
  pattern-matches examples better than prose.
